text: The slaying of Narakasura — the story of Sri Krishna and Satyabhama Long ago there lived a demon king named Narakasura.
He was the son of Bhudevi, Mother Earth.
Narakasura first gained great power, and with that power he began to torment people and the devas.
He attacked many kingdoms and held thousands of princesses captive.
He even stole the earrings of Aditi, the mother of the devas.
Unable to bear Narakasura's cruelty, the devas sought refuge in Sri Krishna.
Then Sri Krishna, together with Satyabhama Devi, set out on Garuda for Pragjyotishapura, Narakasura's kingdom.
There a fierce battle was fought with Narakasura's army.
Sri Krishna broke through Narakasura's defences and defeated his army.
According to the telling well known in the Telugu lands, Satyabhama Devi too fought bravely in the battle.
It is said that Satyabhama, who is seen as a form of Bhudevi, played an important part in the slaying of Narakasura.
But according to the telling in the Bhagavata Purana, it was Sri Krishna himself who slew Narakasura.
With Narakasura's death, the princesses held in his prison were set free.
Sri Krishna won back Aditi's stolen earrings.
With the slaying of Narakasura, the people were freed from fear.
Naraka Chaturdashi is celebrated in remembrance of that victory.
What this story tells us However great one's power may be, if it is used to harm others, a fall is certain in the end.
The slaying of Narakasura reminds us that however strong adharma may seem, dharma wins in the end.
To remove the arrogance, envy and bad thoughts within us, and to move forward with goodness — that is the message this festival gives us.
